candidates.original_title: The CD47-signal regulatory protein alpha (SIRPa) interaction is a therapeutic target for human solid tumors
candidates.description: Anti-CD47 antibody treatment causes short-term anemia without unacceptable toxicity in mice.
candidates.citation_sentence: In 2012, Willingham et al. reported that blocking the signal regulatory protein alpha (SIRPa)/CD47 interaction with an anti-CD47 blocking antibody promoted phagocytosis of solid tumor cells in vitro and reduced growth of solid tumors in vivo indicating that anti-CD47 antibody therapy may be an effective treatment for a variety of solid tumors.
candidates.notes: The replication observed short-term anemia after anti-CD47 treatment, consistent with the toxicity findings reported in the original study. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: The CD47-signal regulatory protein alpha (SIRPa) interaction is a therapeutic target for human solid tumors
candidates.description: Anti-CD47 antibody treatment reduces the final weight of syngeneic breast tumors compared with IgG control treatment.
candidates.citation_sentence: In 2012, Willingham et al. reported that blocking the signal regulatory protein alpha (SIRPa)/CD47 interaction with an anti-CD47 blocking antibody promoted phagocytosis of solid tumor cells in vitro and reduced growth of solid tumors in vivo indicating that anti-CD47 antibody therapy may be an effective treatment for a variety of solid tumors.
candidates.notes: The replication found numerically heavier tumors after anti-CD47 treatment and no statistically significant reduction in tumor weight. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: The CD47-signal regulatory protein alpha (SIRPa) interaction is a therapeutic target for human solid tumors
candidates.description: Anti-CD47 antibody treatment increases lymphocytic infiltration into syngeneic breast tumors.
candidates.citation_sentence: In 2012, Willingham et al. reported that blocking the signal regulatory protein alpha (SIRPa)/CD47 interaction with an anti-CD47 blocking antibody promoted phagocytosis of solid tumor cells in vitro and reduced growth of solid tumors in vivo indicating that anti-CD47 antibody therapy may be an effective treatment for a variety of solid tumors.
candidates.notes: The replication reported minimal to moderate lymphocytic infiltration in both IgG and anti-CD47 tumors, without a clear demonstrated treatment-related increase. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
